title: 8 BORING Machines That Quietly Pay You for Years (No Employees Needed)

speakers.name: Harry (illustrative composite character, does not speak)

promo_conflict: Faceless listicle/narration channel. 'Harry' is a made-up character ('Call him Harry') with suspiciously exact figures ($3,847, $4,317). The ATM figures come from ATM Depot and ATM Marketplace, which are industry guides tied to sellers. Two books are plugged (The 4-Hour Work Week, The Millionaire Next Door), possibly as affiliate links. Everything is based on US rules (FinCEN, state licences).

stated_problem.quote: A crowd that needs cash. Standing somewhere a bank forgot to put a machine.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Independent ATM placement route
idea.one_liner: Buy (or host via a processor) cash machines, place them in cash-heavy shops and bars, and earn the surcharge plus interchange on every withdrawal, shared with the store.
idea.customer: Walk-in consumers who need cash; store owners host the machine
idea.offer: A cash machine at no upfront cost to the store, plus a monthly fee split
idea.revenue_model: Per-withdrawal surcharge ($2.50-$4) plus interchange (10-25c), split with the host or the host gets a flat monthly payment

key_quotes.quote: A regular person owns it, filled it with their own cash, cut a quiet deal with the store, and gets paid every single time somebody hits withdraw.
I will put a cash machine in here at no cost to you.
Door two, a processor supplies the machine and even the cash, and you just find the location and take a slice.

claims.quote: A single well-placed machine in a busy spot can throw off around $1,250 a month.
In fees alone, a sleepy little store might do closer to 500.

claims.claim: A route of 6-12 machines can reach about $10k/month in gross fees (ATM Depot)
claims.quote: And a small route, say 6 to 12 machines, can push toward $10,000 a month in gross fees.
$2.50, sometimes three, sometimes as much as four.
Call it 500 withdrawals in a month at $2.50 each.
usually somewhere between 10 and 25 cents per [music] withdrawal.

claims.claim: Interchange adds $30-$75/month on a busy machine
claims.quote: on a busy machine that is another $30 to $75 a month just appearing.

claims.claim: A machine costs $2,200-$8,000 new; used ones are cheaper
claims.quote: And a machine runs about $2,200 on the low end, up to around $8,000 for a shiny new one.
both peg the payback on a wellplaced machine at somewhere between 6 and 18 months.

claims.claim: The store usually gets about half the surcharge or a flat monthly payment
claims.quote: A common deal hands the store owner something like half the search [music] charge or a flat check every month.

claims.claim: A busy bar machine does 500-600 withdrawals/month
claims.quote: A busy bar with a long line for cash doing 500, even 600 withdrawals in one month.

claims.claim: A forum operator has run a route for more than 7 years
claims.quote: One of them has run his own route for more than 7 years.

claims.claim: Fictional Harry's 8-machine route clears about $4,300 in a strong month
claims.quote: On a strong month, that route clears somewhere around $4,300.
One good machine at $2.50 a toll time 500 tolls a month is about $1,250.

claims.claim: About $600/month per machine after the store split
claims.quote: Keep half of that after the store split and call it a little over $600 a month.

acquisition_channels.details: Scout busy cash-heavy shops on everyday errands, walk in and pitch the owner: 'no upfront cost to you', fee split
Compare offers from processors; under 'door two' the processor supplies the machine and cash and you find the location

ideas.delivery: Operator owns the machine, loads the cash, refills it on a regular loop, and moves dead machines. A processor handles network settlement.
ideas.other_uk_rules: US model. In the UK, independent ATMs run through the LINK network via a sponsoring deployer. Free-to-use ATMs dominate, and LINK and cash-access rules (FSMA 2023) apply. Handling cash may bring Money Laundering Regulations and HMRC/FCA oversight. Pay-to-use surcharges are commercially weak in the UK.

stated_problem.quote: a gas station, a marina, a feed store, a place with no ice freezer of its own.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Ice vending kiosk
idea.one_liner: Install a standalone bagged-ice vending kiosk on a leased pad at a petrol station, marina or campground and sell ice by card.
idea.revenue_model: $1.50-$3 per bag; pad lease $200-$400/month or a share of sales

key_quotes.quote: Steve Slaggel runs Beachside Ice in Panama City Beach, Florida.
Confirm the [music] traffic first, sign the lease first, buy the machine last.

claims.claim: One machine at a petrol station clears about $2,500/month
claims.quote: A single ice machine outside a gas station cleared roughly $2,500 a month for one operator.
On one unit, quiet suburban spots run 700 to,200 a month.

claims.claim: Marina or campground in peak season: $3,500+
claims.quote: a marina or a campground in peak season.
$1.50 to $3 a bag right at the machine.
40 to 60 bags a day is a busy spot.

claims.claim: Beachside Ice started with 2 machines in 2022 and grew to 8
claims.quote: He started with two machines back in early 2022.

claims.claim: Land lease of $200-$400/month or a share of sales
claims.quote: You sign a simple land lease, often $200 to $400 a month for the pad or a small cut of sales.
a standalone kiosk unit runs about $38,000 to $62,000 allin with the pad and the plumbing and the power.

acquisition_channels.details: Negotiate a pad lease with the landlord of a petrol station, marina, feed store or RV park
Existing foot and vehicle traffic at the site

ideas.delivery: Self-contained kiosk makes and bags ice. The operator handles maintenance, plumbing, power and hygiene.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Ice is food, so the business must register as a food business with the local council (food hygiene rules). Planning permission, utility connections and Water Regulations (backflow) also apply. UK demand for ice is weaker and seasonal.

idea.name: Crypto ATM hosting/placement
idea.one_liner: Place an operator network's crypto ATM in a convenience store and split the spread revenue, or own and operate machines.
idea.customer: Walk-in buyers of crypto with cash
idea.revenue_model: Spread on each transaction, split 50/50 or a flat $100/month to the host

key_quotes.quote: this is a placement business, not a bet on any coin [music] price.
You partner with an operator network, place their machine on a store floor, and split the revenue.

claims.quote: A single hosted machine nets roughly $300 to $1,200 a month.
150 to 300 transactions a month is a healthy location.

claims.claim: 50/50 split at a premium spot or a flat $100/month
claims.quote: Often 50/50 at a premium spot or a [music] flat $100 a month at an average one.

claims.claim: Near-zero upfront cost for a host
claims.quote: As a host, your upfront cost can be almost nothing.

claims.claim: About 23 US states require a money transmitter licence
claims.quote: Roughly 23 states want a money transmitter license on top.

acquisition_channels.details: Partner with a crypto ATM operator network
Secure floor space in convenience stores

ideas.delivery: The operator network supplies and runs the kiosk. The host provides the location.

uk_legal_risk.reason: Crypto ATMs are effectively illegal in the UK. The FCA has registered no crypto ATM operator, and running one is a criminal offence (there have been prosecutions).
